identity.real_world_identity_notes: Reiza developed Formula Vee Gen2 with the Brazilian series. Current category material specifies an H-pattern manual, while 2025 regulations identify the Naja01-D chassis and a Volkswagen five-speed gearbox; the exact AMS2 identity and behavior were checked independently.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit inspection showed an open-top yoke-shaped rim without an integrated display or wheel-mounted shift lights.

notes: The clutch is required to move from rest, but correctly rev-matched running shifts were accepted without it.
Full-throttle clutchless upshifts were rejected and succeeded only after a throttle lift; clutchless downshifts were rejected until the driver supplied a manual blip.
Non-adjacent H-pattern inputs directly selected the requested gears.

The gearbox is the longitudinal Volkswagen Gol five-speed the Brazilian regulations mandate, supplied sealed. It is a production road unit and the regulation forbids opening it, so its construction is synchromesh - but no reviewed source says so for this gearbox in particular, and the corroborating Formula Vee rule covers only the air-cooled four-speed, so the value is recorded at medium confidence.

The downshift blip stays as the drive found it: clutchless downshifts were rejected until the driver blipped. A synchromesh does not need a blip to engage, so this is the record's declared departure from the archetype rather than something the construction revises.

Recorded after this field had been left unknown once with the same Brazilian regulation already cited. The reversal is deliberate: the regulation names the unit rather than its construction, and the construction is taken from the unit being an unmodified production road gearbox.
Guided live test completed with Auto Clutch and Auto Shifting disabled.
Standing-start clutch, five direct H selections, required lift/manual blip, and the open yoke rim were directly observed.

confidence.basis: Official series/regulation sources establish the current H-pattern and five-speed architecture, while the exact AMS2 identity and all user-facing technique were directly tested.

claims.basis: Official Reiza and Brazilian-series sources establish the Gen2/current-series context; exact live telemetry establishes the simulator identity.
Official sources and direct five-gear H-pattern selection agree.
Guided current-game A/B tests directly established standing-start clutch, lift/manual-blip requirements, absence of automatic cut/blip, and wheel details.

The Brazilian regulations permit two transmissions and this car runs the second: five gears originating from the longitudinal Gol, supplied sealed by the promoter. The Gol gearbox is a production Volkswagen road unit and the regulation forbids opening it, so the construction is synchromesh. No reviewed source uses that word for this unit, and the corroborating Formula Vee regulation covers only the air-cooled Type 1 and 3 four-speed, so this is inferred from the unit rather than stated by a source and sits at medium.

deviations.basis: The driver must blip on downshifts, where the archetype leaves it optional. The value came from a guided drive that rejected a clutchless downshift without one. It sits oddly with a synchromesh, which does not need a blip to engage, and that tension is left standing rather than resolved: the construction is only a medium-confidence claim and cannot overrule a drive.

notes: Gearbox construction remains unknown rather than being inferred from successful rev-matched clutchless shifts.
